_comment: Consolidated KB used by alpha_generator.py and math_engine.py. Treats Brain as a formal expression language. Operator/field whitelists live in data/brain_docs/operators.json and fields.json (data-driven). This file holds: language primer, fitness targets, exemplars, archetype hints, and risk heuristics learned from past submissions.

language_primer.what_an_alpha_is: An alpha is a daily, per-stock numeric vector. Brain re-evaluates the expression each trading day for every stock in the universe. Positive values become longs, negatives become shorts; magnitudes become weights. The vector is automatically (a) winsorized/truncated to settings.truncation, (b) neutralized per settings.neutralization (Market/Sector/Industry/Subindustry), (c) smoothed by settings.decay, and (d) book-sized to $20M long + $20M short. You do NOT need scale() unless you want explicit L1 normalization on top of Brain's auto-normalization.
language_primer.evaluation_model: Expression is a pure function of cross-sectional vectors. Operators fall into 4 broad classes: (1) elementwise/arithmetic (a+b, a*b, abs, log, sign, signed_power, pow); (2) cross-sectional (rank, zscore, normalize, quantile, scale, winsorize); (3) time-series (ts_mean, ts_sum, ts_std_dev, ts_delta, ts_corr, ts_covariance, ts_rank, ts_max, ts_min, ts_arg_max, ts_arg_min, ts_decay_linear, ts_product, ts_zscore); (4) group/sector (group_neutralize, group_rank, group_mean, group_zscore).

settings_shape_the_portfolio.universe: Which stocks are eligible (TOP3000, TOP1000, TOP500, TOP200).
settings_shape_the_portfolio.neutralization: Subtract the group mean. Market = no group, just demean. Sector/Industry/Subindustry = demean within group. If group_neutralize() is INSIDE the expression, set neutralization=Market to avoid double demeaning.
settings_shape_the_portfolio.decay: Exponential smoothing in days. Higher decay = lower turnover, smaller daily reallocation. Decay 0 = no smoothing.
settings_shape_the_portfolio.truncation: Max weight per stock (0.01 to 0.10). Lower = more diversified.
settings_shape_the_portfolio.delay: Trading lag. delay=1 = trade tomorrow's open on data through end-of-day T-1 (the safe default, supports the FULL field catalog). delay=0 = trade today's close on data through today (supports a SMALLER field catalog: intraday price/volume, options IV, vector/sentiment data, and a subset of fundamentals; USA region only in this codebase). Choose delay=0 only when the mechanism is genuinely intraday (signal IS today's close-vs-vwap divergence, today's options skew, etc.) OR when the signal is slow-moving but you need same-day execution to capture the edge before it dissipates. Choose delay=1 for fundamental/analyst/slow-moving mechanisms that don't need same-day execution. See confirmed_working examples tagged d0_* for D0 templates.

language_primer.fitness: Sharpe * sqrt(|Returns| / max(Turnover, 0.125)). Brain's is.turnover is a fraction in [0,1] (0.6232 = 62.32% daily turnover); multiply by 100 to get a percentage value.
language_primer.scale_is_optional: scale() L1-normalizes so sum(|weights|)=1. It is NOT required as the outer wrapper. Most 101 Formulaic Alphas end in rank(...) or (-1 * rank(...)) with no scale(). Use scale() only when you need a specific normalization that Brain's auto-pipeline won't provide.

fitness_formula.notes: Brain's is.turnover is a fraction in [0,1]: 0.6232 = 62.32% daily turnover. Multiply by 100 to compare against percent targets.

confirmed_working.name: lottery_plus_volume
confirmed_working.logic: Negative cubic moment (lottery aversion) gated by volume surge. group_neutralize inside forces panel=Market. Volume ratio remains unit-consistent.

confirmed_working.name: volcorr_reversal
confirmed_working.logic: Negative 10-day correlation of returns and volume signals overextension. Note: no outer scale() needed.

confirmed_working.name: price_plus_volsurge
confirmed_working.logic: 1-day reversal normalized by long-run price, gated by short-vs-long volume surge. Ratios remain unit-consistent.

confirmed_working.name: roa_quality
confirmed_working.logic: Operating profitability (ROA proxy) z-scored within trailing window. Long high-margin operators, short low-margin. Replaces ev_ebitda exemplar which used the invalid enterprise_value field.

confirmed_working.name: vwap_premium
confirmed_working.logic: Stocks closing above VWAP are overextended intraday — short them. Ratio remains unit-consistent.

confirmed_working.name: alpha101_001_fixed
confirmed_working.logic: 101 Formulaic Alphas-style construct fixed for unit consistency (abs(returns) in else branch, not close) and smoothed with ts_decay_linear to lift fitness. Replaces broken alpha101_001_style which mixed CSPrice and unitless branches in if_else and produced LOW_FITNESS (0.74).

confirmed_working.name: d0_vwap_intraday_reversion
confirmed_working.logic: DELAY 0 USA. Same-day intraday-reversion off VWAP, gated by intraday range (high/low). The mechanism only fires when you can trade after seeing the close — cannot work at delay=1 because the signal IS today's close-vs-vwap divergence.

confirmed_working.name: d0_options_iv_skew
confirmed_working.logic: DELAY 0 USA. Options-implied volatility skew (call IV minus put IV) captures same-day positioning asymmetry. Call IV > put IV signals bullish positioning. Works at delay=0 because the IV surface revalues intraday and the edge decays overnight.

confirmed_working.name: d0_ebit_capex_low_turnover
confirmed_working.logic: DELAY 0 USA. Capital-efficient firms (low ebit/capex inverted to long high-capex-relative-to-earnings) generate stable D0 edge with only 2.36% turnover. Proves FUNDAMENTAL ratios CAN run at delay=0 — the data is available at D0 and the slow signal benefits from immediate execution. Real submission: Sharpe 2.02, Fitness 2.30, Returns 16.15%.

confirmed_working.name: d0_ev_ebitda_valuation_reversion
confirmed_working.logic: DELAY 0 USA. EV/EBITDA valuation reversion z-scored over 63 days. Second proof point that fundamental ratios run at D0. NOTE: enterprise_value is on this codebase's forbidden_fields list at D1 — it may behave differently at D0. Real submission: Sharpe 2.58, Fitness 1.70, Turnover 26.63%.

confirmed_failing.reason: static portfolio: 252-day std_dev alone produces near-zero daily turnover
positive cubic moment with zscore — buys lottery stocks (anti-pattern)
invalid Brain syntax — SMA is not a Brain operator (TA-Lib)
bare quadratic returns as primary signal: zero-mean variance proxy without cubic skew direction
raw volume as primary signal biases towards large-cap mega stocks

if_else mixes a unitless branch (ts_std_dev(returns,20)) with a CSPrice branch (close) → Brain UNITS warning. Also: ts_arg_max over a 5-day window with no smoothing produces a coarse signal → LOW_FITNESS (0.74 < 1.0).
enterprise_value is not a Brain data field — submission would fail at parse time. Use sharesout*close as market cap proxy instead.
Division by ts_mean(volume,60) is unit-consistent. Do not add scalar epsilons like +1 under unitHandling=VERIFY; instead keep the ratio bounded with rank()/zscore().

reversal.intuition: Short-horizon mean reversion in returns / overextension signaled by price-volume comovement.

fundamental.intuition: Valuation, profitability, leverage, or accruals — slow-moving, sector-neutralized.

volatility.intuition: Cross-sectional dispersion or persistence of realized volatility.

analyst_revision.intuition: Analyst-estimate revisions (anl4_eps_rev_*, analyst_revision_rank_derivative, consensus_*) drift over weeks to months. The classic mechanism: when sell-side analysts revise EPS or sales estimates up, the stock under-reacts initially and drifts in the same direction (PEAD-style). Pair the revision with a quality filter (ebit/assets) so the long leg is profitable revisions, not bottom-fishing junk being upgraded. Avoid price-only momentum — the edge is in the analyst signal, not the recent return.

earnings_event.intuition: Post-earnings-announcement drift (PEAD). Earnings surprise predicts subsequent return for several weeks (Ball & Brown 1968; Bernard & Thomas 1989). REAL FIELDS VERIFIED IN CATALOG: abnormal_return_earnings_release, change_in_eps_surprise, sales_surprise_score (NOT 'sales_surprise' — append the _score suffix), and the mdl177_2_surpriseanalystmodel_qsa_* family (composite, efficiency, percent, etc.). DO NOT use earnings_certainty_rank_derivative as the primary leg — it is a STATIC analyst-confidence score, not an event signal, and has produced near-zero edge across 19 historical sims. DO NOT use bare names 'eps_surprise' or 'sales_surprise' — those don't exist; you need the full prefixed name. If you cannot find a true PEAD field for the candidate, route the alpha to a different archetype instead of forcing this one.

microstructure.intuition: Intraday order-flow imbalance and tape-reading. Signals: close-vwap (where did the day close relative to VWAP — buying pressure?), open-close gap and reversion, ts_corr(returns, volume, 3-10) for short-window confirmation, dollar-volume bursts. This is DIFFERENT from reversal: microstructure operates over hours-to-days on intraday-level price action, not multi-day mean reversion. Pair with liquidity normalization (rank(volume / ts_mean(volume, 60))) so the signal is concentrated in tradable names.

options_implied.intuition: Options-implied signals — entirely unmined in our pool. The options market prices forward-looking risk and asymmetric outcomes that the underlying price tape cannot capture. REAL FIELDS VERIFIED IN CATALOG: implied_volatility_call_{10,20,30,60,90,120,180,270,360,720,1080}, implied_volatility_put_{same}, out_of_money_put_call_ratio. DO NOT use option_skew, option_term, skew_ratio — those do NOT exist in the catalog and will error with 'unknown variable'. Key mechanisms: (a) put-call implied-vol SKEW (rank(implied_volatility_put_30 - implied_volatility_call_30)) captures fear/greed asymmetry, (b) term-structure spread (rank(implied_volatility_call_30 - implied_volatility_call_180)) captures near-vs-far uncertainty, (c) implied vs realized vol gap (rank(implied_volatility_call_30 / (ts_std_dev(returns, 21) + 0.0001))) captures vol risk premium, (d) out_of_money_put_call_ratio as a sentiment leg. These are NEVER PASSED — first novel-family wins in this space have the highest expected lift.

factor_residual.intuition: Residual alpha AFTER removing sector / industry / factor exposures. The principle: most alphas measure 'momentum' or 'mean-reversion' but most of that signal is already absorbed by sector or market factor exposure. The RESIDUAL — what's left after subtracting the sector-cross-section average — is genuinely idiosyncratic alpha. CRITICAL OPERATOR ARITY (verified against operators.json): group_zscore(x, group) takes EXACTLY 2 args; group_neutralize(x, group) takes EXACTLY 2 args; group_rank(x, group) takes EXACTLY 2 args. group_mean(x, weight, group) takes EXACTLY 3 args — DO NOT write group_mean(x, sector); BRAIN will error with 'Invalid number of inputs'. Build the residual via the 2-arg operators: `group_zscore(X, sector)` to get a fully-residualized signal, or `X - group_neutralize(X, sector)` which extracts the group-mean component. Pair with a non-residual signal as cross-leg. The mechanism is DIFFERENT from group_neutralize-WRAPPING the whole expression — that's a NORMALIZATION step; this is using group_zscore as the inner mechanism that exposes cross-sectional residual directly.

dispersion.intuition: Cross-sectional or time-series DISPERSION as the signal — not the level. REAL FIELDS VERIFIED IN CATALOG (only 4 dispersion fields exist!): fy1_eps_estimate_dispersion_2, fy1_eps_estimate_dispersion_globaldividend, fy2_eps_estimate_dispersion, sales_estimate_dispersion. DO NOT use anl4_eps_estimate_std or anl4_eps_estimate_mean — those do NOT exist; the catalog only has the dispersion FIELD already pre-computed. Trade direction: high analyst dispersion typically signals UNDERPERFORMANCE (Diether et al. 2002) — short high-dispersion, long low-dispersion. Build via: rank(-fy1_eps_estimate_dispersion_2) as the primary leg, paired with quality (ebit/assets) or revision (analyst_revision_rank_derivative). For time-series-dispersion mechanisms, you can use ts_std_dev(implied_volatility_call_30, 21) since the IV field IS in the catalog. NOT the same as `volatility` — that archetype uses raw vol levels; this archetype uses VARIATION OF estimates/levels.

novel.intuition: Catch-all for compound or unusual structures (e.g. lottery aversion, residual-of-residual neutralization, options-implied skew patterns, alt-data composites that don't map cleanly to the other six archetypes). REQUIRED to be genuinely novel — not a repackaged Parkinson volatility or simple ts_delta(close, N) under a new name.

_archetype_note: Seven top-level archetypes match the generator prompt. Anything not fitting cleanly is 'novel'. math_engine.predict_archetype returns the best-matching archetype by signature token count and falls back to 'novel'. Momentum archetype was removed in May 2026 — 0/77 historical passes made it not worth the BRAIN-slot cost.
_forbidden_note: TA-Lib operators (SMA, EMA, ...) do NOT exist in Brain. The Python builtins (float) and the misspellings (winsorize is pandas/scipy; decay_linear should be ts_decay_linear; ts_ir does not exist) are also blacklisted. All OTHER operator validation is data-driven from data/brain_docs/operators.json.
_forbidden_fields_note: These names exist in many quant references but are NOT Brain data fields. Use sharesout*close for market cap, ts_mean(volume,N) for dollar volume, and ebit/ebitda/sales for fundamentals. The trailing entries (vol_expansion_ratio, vwap_deviation, debt_change_ratio, close_delta_1_vwap, short_returns_mean, quality_decay) are mechanism-FAMILY taxonomy LABELS from math_engine._MECHANISM_FAMILIES — the LLM kept copying them out of the prompt's family tables as if they were fields, so the local gate now rejects them on attempt 1 instead of burning the whole round.

risk_heuristics.description: returns*returns appearing without a third multiplication AND as the dominant signal creates a directionless variance proxy. Cubic (returns*returns*returns with negation) is the proven direction. Allowed inside ts_corr / ts_covariance.
risk_heuristics.applies_when: returns*returns is the primary signal, not embedded in a correlation

risk_heuristics.description: Positive cubic moment buys lottery-like stocks (empirically negative Sharpe). Negate it.
Raw volume as the primary signal biases toward mega-caps. Normalize by ts_mean(volume, N) or use volume only inside ts_corr/ts_covariance.
ts_delta(close, N) without /close or /ts_mean(close, M) is dollar-denominated and dominated by share-price levels.
group_neutralize inside expression — neutralization must be Market to avoid double demean.
ts_std_dev(returns, d>=200) alone produces near-zero daily turnover. Combine with a daily-varying signal or use a shorter window.
Decay below 4 produces high turnover. Suggest decay >= 4 unless intentional (e.g. fast reversal alphas).
Time-series operators require a day-window argument: ts_mean(x, d), not ts_mean(x). Syntax error.
zscore() takes exactly one argument. Multi-arg form is invalid syntax.
TA-Lib operators (SMA, EMA, RSI, MACD, etc.) are not Brain operators.
Operator name not found in data/brain_docs/operators.json. May indicate typo or unseeded operator.
Predicted turnover outside 1-70% target band (Brain fitness penalizes the high end; below 1% the alpha has effectively no daily activity).
if_else / max / min branches have incompatible units (e.g. price vs unitless). Brain emits a UNITS warning and the alpha cannot be submitted. Normalize both branches to the same unit.
Estimated fitness (archetype Sharpe midpoint x sqrt(returns/turnover)) below the 1.0 submission floor. Add ts_decay_linear, extend windows, or raise decay.
ts_arg_max / ts_arg_min over a window <= 9 produces only a handful of distinct integer values. Without ts_decay_linear or high decay, the resulting signal is coarse and fitness suffers.
Field name is not a real Brain data field (e.g. enterprise_value, cap, adv20, adv60, fnd6_*, industry). Submission will fail at parse time. Use the valid set in data/brain_docs/fields.json.
Division `a / b` where b is a Brain field or ts_* call. Keep ratios unit-consistent under unitHandling=VERIFY: do not add scalar epsilons like +1 or +0.001 to price/share/fundamental denominators.
